class_lesson.concept_statement: You will identify a triangle's base and height.
class_lesson.goal: You will choose a triangle's base and match its straight height.

techniques.name: Choose and Check
techniques.purpose: Use this method when choosing a matching base and height.

steps.detail: Choose one side of the triangle as the base.
Find the opposite corner above the chosen base.
Trace the shortest straight line from the corner to the base.
Check that the height meets the base squarely.

techniques.example: For base $AB$, the matching height meets $AB$ at a square corner.
techniques.why_it_matters: The check gives the correct height for the chosen base.
techniques.common_error: Learners choose a sloping side because it looks longer.

techniques.name: Extend and Match
techniques.purpose: Use this when the height meets outside the triangle.

steps.detail: Choose the side that will act as the base.
Continue the base line beyond the triangle when needed.
Find the straight line from the opposite corner.
Make sure both lines meet at a square corner.

techniques.example: Base $AB$ may extend to $D$, where height $CD$ meets squarely.
techniques.why_it_matters: You can identify heights that lie outside sloping triangles.
techniques.common_error: Learners stop at the triangle's edge and choose a sloping side.

worked_examples.title: Height inside the triangle
worked_examples.input: In triangle $ABC$, sides $AB$ and $AC$ meet at a square corner. Choose $AB$ as the base. Identify the matching height.
worked_examples.decoding: I must find the straight distance from $C$ to base $AB$.
worked_examples.plan: Use Choose and Check because the height lies inside.
worked_examples.model_answer: First, choose $AB$ as the base. The opposite corner is $C$. Look for the straight line from $C$ to $AB$. Side $AC$ reaches $AB$ at $A$. The corner at $A$ is square. Therefore, $AC$ is the matching height. The base is $AB$, and the height is $AC$.

annotations.comment: The chosen base decides which height must be used.
The matching height starts from the opposite corner.
A height must meet its base at a square corner.

worked_examples.title: Height outside the triangle
worked_examples.input: In triangle $ABC$, choose $AB$ as the base. The line $AB$ continues past $B$ to $D$. Line $CD$ meets the continued base at a square corner. Identify the matching height.
worked_examples.decoding: I must find the straight height, even though it lies outside.
worked_examples.plan: Use Extend and Match because the triangle is sloping.
worked_examples.model_answer: First, choose $AB$ as the base. Continue its line from $B$ to $D$. The opposite corner is $C$. Line $CD$ reaches the continued base at $D$. The corner at $D$ is square. Therefore, $CD$ is the matching height. The base is $AB$, and the height is $CD$.

annotations.comment: A base may be extended to meet the height.
The height may fall outside a sloping triangle.
This confirms that $CD$ is the straight height.

worked_examples.title: A different chosen base
worked_examples.input: In triangle $PQR$, line $QS$ meets side $PR$ at a square corner. Choose $PR$ as the base. Identify the matching height.
worked_examples.decoding: I must match base $PR$ with its square-meeting line.
worked_examples.plan: Use Choose and Check to test the line from $Q$.
worked_examples.model_answer: First, choose $PR$ as the base. The opposite corner is $Q$. Line $QS$ goes from $Q$ to base $PR$. It meets $PR$ at $S$. The corner at $S$ is square. Therefore, $QS$ is the matching height. The base is $PR$, and the height is $QS$.

annotations.comment: The height starts from the corner opposite the base.
The height must reach the chosen base line.
This square corner proves the base and height match.

class_lesson.concept_statement: You will use the triangle area formula correctly.
class_lesson.goal: You will correctly use the triangle area formula to find area.

techniques.name: Write, Substitute, Halve
techniques.purpose: Use this method when the base and matching height are given.

steps.detail: Write $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.
Replace the words with the given base and height.
Halve one even factor before multiplying the numbers.
Multiply the remaining factors to find the area.
State the triangle's area using the correct square unit.

techniques.why_it_matters: The ordered steps include the half and prevent skipped working.
techniques.common_error: Learners sometimes multiply the base and height without halving.

techniques.name: Multiply, Then Divide
techniques.purpose: Use this method when neither base nor height is even.

steps.detail: Write $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.
Put the given base and height into the formula.
Multiply the base and height before finding one half.
Divide the product by $2$ without rounding it.
State the exact area using the correct square unit.

techniques.why_it_matters: This method gives an exact answer when both factors are odd.
techniques.common_error: Learners sometimes round an odd product instead of halving exactly.

worked_examples.title: Halve the base first
worked_examples.input: Find the area of a triangle with base $14$ cm and height $9$ cm.
worked_examples.decoding: I need half the product of $14$ and $9$.
worked_examples.plan: Use Write, Substitute, Halve because both lengths are given.
worked_examples.model_answer: Write the formula. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$. Substitute the given lengths. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 14 \times 9$. Halve the even base first. $14 \div 2 = 7$. Now multiply. $\text{Area} = 7 \times 9 = 63\text{ cm}^2$. The triangle's area is $63\text{ cm}^2$.

annotations.comment: The base and height replace the words in the formula.
Only one factor is halved before multiplying.
This multiplication gives half the related rectangle's area.

worked_examples.title: Halve the height first
worked_examples.input: Find the area of a triangle with base $15$ m and height $8$ m.
worked_examples.decoding: I need half the product of $15$ and $8$.
worked_examples.plan: Use Write, Substitute, Halve and halve the even height.
worked_examples.model_answer: Write the formula. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$. Substitute the given lengths. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 15 \times 8$. Halve the even height first. $8 \div 2 = 4$. Now multiply. $\text{Area} = 15 \times 4 = 60\text{ m}^2$. The triangle's area is $60\text{ m}^2$.

annotations.comment: The formula shows that the product must be halved.
The even height is easier to halve than $15$.
The remaining factors give the triangle's area.

worked_examples.title: Both lengths are odd
worked_examples.input: Find the area of a triangle with base $9$ cm and height $7$ cm.
worked_examples.decoding: I need half the product of $9$ and $7$.
worked_examples.plan: Use Multiply, Then Divide because both factors are odd.
worked_examples.model_answer: Write the formula. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$. Substitute the given lengths. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 7$. Neither factor is even, so multiply first. $9 \times 7 = 63$. Now divide the product by $2$. $63 \div 2 = 31.5$. Therefore, $\text{Area} = 31.5\text{ cm}^2$. The triangle's area is $31.5\text{ cm}^2$.

annotations.comment: The one-half remains visible in the formula.
Multiplying first works because both factors are odd.
The odd product gives an exact decimal area.
The exact answer is kept instead of being rounded.

worked_examples.title: An odd product in metres
worked_examples.input: Find the area of a triangle with base $5$ m and height $11$ m.
worked_examples.decoding: I need half the product of $5$ and $11$.
worked_examples.plan: Use Multiply, Then Divide because neither factor is even.
worked_examples.model_answer: Write the formula. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$. Substitute the given lengths. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 11$. Multiply the two lengths first. $5 \times 11 = 55$. Divide the product by $2$. $55 \div 2 = 27.5$. Therefore, $\text{Area} = 27.5\text{ m}^2$. The triangle's area is $27.5\text{ m}^2$.

annotations.comment: The formula uses the given base and height once.
The base and height form an odd product.
Dividing by $2$ correctly applies the one-half.
The decimal is the exact area of the triangle.

class_lesson.concept_statement: You will find half a related rectangle's area.
class_lesson.goal: You will find a triangle's area by halving its related rectangle.

techniques.name: Rectangle then half
techniques.purpose: Use this when a triangle fills half a related rectangle.

steps.detail: Multiply the rectangle's base by its height.
Divide the rectangle's area by $2$.
Write the triangle's answer using square units.

techniques.example: A $6$ by $5$ rectangle has area $6 \times 5 = 30$ square units, so the triangle has area $30 \div 2 = 15$ square units.
techniques.why_it_matters: It shows why the triangle uses half the rectangle.
techniques.common_error: Learners sometimes give the whole rectangle's area as the triangle's area.

techniques.name: Halve before multiplying
techniques.purpose: Use this when one rectangle side is an even number.

steps.detail: Find the side that can divide evenly by $2$.
Divide only that side by $2$.
Multiply the halved side by the other side.
Write the final area using square units.

techniques.example: For a $12$ by $7$ rectangle, use $12 \div 2 = 6$, then $6 \times 7 = 42$ square units.
techniques.why_it_matters: The numbers stay smaller and easier to multiply.
techniques.common_error: Learners sometimes halve both sides, making the answer too small.

worked_examples.title: Half of a six-by-five rectangle
worked_examples.input: A triangle fills half a $6$ by $5$ rectangle. Find its area.
worked_examples.decoding: I need half the area of the whole rectangle.
worked_examples.plan: Use Rectangle then half because the triangle fills one half.
worked_examples.model_answer: First find the related rectangle's area. $6 \times 5 = 30$ square units. The triangle fills half the rectangle. $30 \div 2 = 15$ square units. The triangle's area is $15$ square units.

annotations.comment: This finds the area of the whole related rectangle.
Dividing by $2$ finds one of two equal halves.

annotations.part: The triangle's area is $15$ square units.
annotations.comment: The final sentence clearly states the required area.

worked_examples.title: Half of a twelve-by-seven rectangle
worked_examples.input: A triangle is half of a $12$ cm by $7$ cm rectangle. Find its area.
worked_examples.decoding: I need one half of the rectangle's area.
worked_examples.plan: Use Halve before multiplying because $12$ is even.
worked_examples.model_answer: The related rectangle measures $12$ cm by $7$ cm. Halve the even side first. $12 \div 2 = 6$. Now multiply by the other side. $6 \times 7 = 42\text{ cm}^2$. The triangle's area is $42\text{ cm}^2$.

annotations.comment: Halving one side gives half the rectangle's area.
This multiplies using smaller and easier numbers.
Square centimetres show that the answer measures area.

worked_examples.title: Correcting the whole-rectangle answer
worked_examples.input: Noah says half of an $8$ cm by $9$ cm rectangle has area $72\text{ cm}^2$. Is he correct?
worked_examples.decoding: I must check whether Noah remembered to take half.
worked_examples.plan: Use Rectangle then half to compare his answer correctly.
worked_examples.model_answer: First find the whole rectangle's area. $8 \times 9 = 72\text{ cm}^2$. Noah used the whole rectangle's area. The triangle needs half that area. $72 \div 2 = 36\text{ cm}^2$. Noah is not correct. The triangle's area is $36\text{ cm}^2$.

annotations.comment: This answer belongs to the whole rectangle.
This missing step changes the rectangle area into half.
This directly answers the question before stating the area.

class_lesson.concept_statement: You will solve simple area word problems.
class_lesson.goal: You will find a triangle's area from a simple story.

techniques.name: Read, Pick, Solve
techniques.purpose: Use this when a word problem gives a triangle's measurements.

steps.detail: Find what triangle area the question asks for.
Write down the given base and matching height.
Use $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.
Substitute the measurements, multiply, and take one half.
State the answer in words with square units.

techniques.example: Base $14$ m and height $6$ m give $\frac{1}{2} \times 14 \times 6 = 42\text{ m}^2$.
techniques.why_it_matters: It turns the story into clear and complete maths.
techniques.common_error: Learners multiply every number mentioned, even unrelated numbers.

techniques.name: Rectangle Then Half
techniques.purpose: Use this when the story describes half a rectangle.

steps.detail: Multiply the shared base and height.
Divide the rectangle's area by $2$.
Use the square unit named in the question.
Connect the final area to the object.

techniques.example: A $16$ m by $5$ m rectangle has area $80\text{ m}^2$, so half is $40\text{ m}^2$.
techniques.why_it_matters: It shows which part of the story must be halved.
techniques.common_error: Learners give the full rectangle's area as the triangle's area.

worked_examples.title: Triangular Flower Bed
worked_examples.input: A triangular flower bed has base $14$ m and height $6$ m. What is its area?
worked_examples.decoding: I need the area inside the triangular flower bed.
worked_examples.plan: Use Read, Pick, Solve because both measurements are given.
worked_examples.model_answer: The base is $14$ m. The height is $6$ m. Use the triangle area rule. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$. Put in the measurements. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 14 \times 6$. Halve $14$ first. $\text{Area} = 7 \times 6 = 42\text{ m}^2$. The flower bed's area is $42\text{ m}^2$.

annotations.part: The base is $14$ m. The height is $6$ m.
annotations.comment: These are the facts needed for the area.
The measurements replace the words in the rule.
Halving $14$ first makes multiplication easier.

annotations.part: The flower bed's area is $42\text{ m}^2$.
annotations.comment: The final sentence answers the story directly.

worked_examples.title: Half of a Playground
worked_examples.input: A rectangular playground is $16$ m long and $5$ m wide. Half of it is a triangular sandpit. What is the sandpit's area?
worked_examples.decoding: I need half the area of the rectangular playground.
worked_examples.plan: Use Rectangle Then Half because the sandpit covers half.
worked_examples.model_answer: First find the playground's full area. $16 \times 5 = 80\text{ m}^2$. The triangular sandpit covers half the playground. $80 \div 2 = 40\text{ m}^2$. The sandpit's area is $40\text{ m}^2$.

annotations.comment: This finds the whole rectangular playground.
The word half tells us to divide by $2$.
This names the object and includes square metres.

worked_examples.title: Triangular Festival Flag
worked_examples.input: A triangular festival flag has base $18$ cm and height $7$ cm. Find the area of cloth used.
worked_examples.decoding: The cloth used is the area inside the triangle.
worked_examples.plan: Use Read, Pick, Solve because the needed facts appear directly.
worked_examples.model_answer: The flag's base is $18$ cm. Its height is $7$ cm. Use the triangle area rule. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 18 \times 7$. Halve $18$ first. $\text{Area} = 9 \times 7 = 63\text{ cm}^2$. The area of cloth used is $63\text{ cm}^2$.

annotations.part: The cloth used is the area inside the triangle.
annotations.comment: This changes the story words into a maths goal.
Only the base and height enter the calculation.
Only one factor is halved before multiplying.

annotations.part: The area of cloth used is $63\text{ cm}^2$.
annotations.comment: The answer uses the wording from the question.

class_lesson.concept_statement: You will check units and spot common errors.
class_lesson.goal: You will check triangle-area answers and correct common errors.

techniques.name: Five-point error sweep
techniques.purpose: Use this after completing or checking a triangle-area solution.

steps.detail: Confirm the base and height form a matching pair.
Make sure the working takes half exactly once.
Repeat the multiplication and division to test them.
Confirm the triangle is half its related rectangle.
Write a square unit after the final area.

techniques.why_it_matters: The sweep catches errors before the answer is finished.
techniques.common_error: Learners check the multiplication but forget the half or unit.

techniques.name: Rectangle half-check
techniques.purpose: Use this when an area answer seems too large or small.

steps.detail: Multiply the same base and height.
Divide the rectangle's area by $2$.
Check that both triangle answers are equal.
Finish with the correct square unit.

techniques.example: The rectangle is $12 \times 6 = 72\text{ m}^2$, so the triangle is $72 \div 2 = 36\text{ m}^2$.
techniques.why_it_matters: This check quickly finds forgotten or repeated halving.
techniques.common_error: Learners accept the full rectangle's area as the triangle's area.

techniques.name: Unit meaning check
techniques.purpose: Use this when checking how an area answer is labelled.

steps.detail: Decide whether the answer measures length or area.
Use square units because area covers a surface.
Keep centimetres, metres, or another given unit.

techniques.example: Lengths in centimetres give an area in $\text{cm}^2$.
techniques.why_it_matters: The correct unit shows that the answer measures area.

worked_examples.title: Forgotten half and wrong unit
worked_examples.input: Leo says a triangle with base $8$ cm and height $5$ cm has area $40$ cm. Find and correct his errors.
worked_examples.decoding: I must check Leo's working, answer size, and unit.
worked_examples.plan: Use the five-point error sweep to find every mistake.
worked_examples.model_answer: First check Leo's product. $8 \times 5 = 40$. This is the related rectangle's area. Leo forgot to take half. $40 \div 2 = 20$. Next check the unit. Area needs square centimetres, not centimetres. The corrected result is $20\text{ cm}^2$. Leo made two errors. The triangle's area is $20\text{ cm}^2$.

annotations.comment: This product gives the whole related rectangle.
The division finds the triangle's half.
Square centimetres show that the answer is an area.

worked_examples.title: Halving both lengths
worked_examples.input: Ava finds the area of a triangle with base $10$ cm and height $8$ cm. She writes $10 \div 2 = 5$, $8 \div 2 = 4$, and $5 \times 4 = 20\text{ cm}^2$. Is she correct?
worked_examples.decoding: I must check whether Ava took half correctly.
worked_examples.plan: Use the rectangle half-check to compare her answer.
worked_examples.model_answer: Find the related rectangle's area first. $10 \times 8 = 80\text{ cm}^2$. The triangle must have half this area. $80 \div 2 = 40\text{ cm}^2$. Ava divided both lengths by $2$. This took half twice. Her answer became one quarter of the rectangle. Ava is not correct. The triangle's area is $40\text{ cm}^2$.

annotations.comment: This gives the full related rectangle's area.
Only one division by $2$ is needed.
Halving both factors makes the result four times smaller.

worked_examples.title: Correct number but incorrect label
worked_examples.input: Noah calculates a triangle's area as $6 \times 7 = 42$, then $42 \div 2 = 21\text{ m}$. Is his final answer correct?
worked_examples.decoding: I must check both the number and its unit.
worked_examples.plan: Use the unit meaning check after checking the calculation.
worked_examples.model_answer: First check the number. $6 \times 7 = 42$. Then take half. $42 \div 2 = 21$. The number $21$ is correct. Now check the unit. Metres measure length, but this answer measures area. The unit must be square metres. Noah's label is incorrect. The triangle's area is $21\text{ m}^2$.

annotations.comment: The calculation correctly finds half the rectangle.
Metres alone measure a one-dimensional length.
Square metres correctly label the covered area.
